title: Arrays and hashing
subtitle: O(n) with a map
briefing: When a nested loop is scanning for a complement or a duplicate, a hash map turns it into one pass. Most paths start here.

title: Two pointers and sliding window
subtitle: Shrink and expand
briefing: Sorted arrays and substrings with a constraint are almost never brute force. Name the window invariant before you code.

title: Lists, stacks, queues
subtitle: Pointers and matching
briefing: Dummy heads, Floyd cycle, and a stack for matching or next-greater. Clean pointer code is scored.

title: Binary search
subtitle: On indexes and on answers
briefing: If the predicate is monotonic, binary search. Rotated arrays and 'minimum feasible capacity' are the usual variants.

title: Binary trees I
subtitle: What does this node return?
briefing: Trees show up constantly. Recursive DFS plus level-order BFS. Practice both.

title: Binary trees II
subtitle: BST, LCA, construct
briefing: Validate a BST with bounds, not just left < root < right on one node. Construction from traversals is a common onsite.

title: Graphs and grids
subtitle: BFS, DFS, indegree
briefing: Number of islands and rotting oranges show up constantly. Multi-source BFS and cycle detection via indegree.

title: Heaps and intervals
subtitle: Top-K and sort-then-scan
briefing: Heap for streaming top-K. Intervals: sort, then one scan. Meeting rooms is the same scan with a heap.

title: Textbook DP
subtitle: Define dp[i], then fill
briefing: Textbook DP is recognizable medium: stairs, robber, coin change, unique paths, LIS, word break. Not burst balloons.

title: Design and hard-adjacent
subtitle: Caches, tries, water
briefing: LRU cache and tries are 'implement this'. Trapping rain water and sliding window maximum are the hard-pattern interviews.

title: Mixed set
subtitle: Name the pattern in two minutes
briefing: No topic labels. Identify the pattern, then code. Weekend: two 45-minute problems back to back.

title: Mocks and weak spots
subtitle: OA simulation
briefing: Re-solve anything you needed a hint on. Two timed problems. Edge cases before you say you are done.
